LESSON: READING 6.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: SONGS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are songs similar to poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies
2. use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies
3. appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 6.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: SONGS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 6.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: SONGS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies

What this means
In this part you learn to identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs to a partner. (skill: use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are songs similar to poems?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies.
5. Be able to: use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies, pick out key messages communicated in lullabies.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
